note: read through zarr directly - dask and the xarray cache both distort this measurement
verdict: Do not tile. The best case, 180x360 plain, buys 19 ms on a Europe cut of t and costs 0.26 s of full read, 2.5 s of write and 15x the files; across all 9 variables the cut is not faster at all (0.286 vs 0.300 s). Decode was never the bottleneck: 213 MB of t decodes in 67 ms, which is 3.2 GB/s. Sharding is strictly worse than plain tiles on every read and only wins back the file count, so on a local disk it buys nothing here. It would be the right tool against object storage, where 4437 GETs versus 297 is the whole cost.
where_the_time_actually_goes: read_bench.py measured the Europe cut at 0.49 s through xr.open_zarr, which hands back dask arrays. The same cut through zarr directly is 0.30 s. Roughly 40% of what looked like decode cost is the dask graph. The slicing endpoint should read with chunks=None or through zarr, not through the default dask path.
